mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month indicates weakening labor market conditions, which leads to reduced consumer spending and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening economy, which leads to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a month signals strengthening supply-side conditions, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the positive signal.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 1.2 million units and consumer spending (RSAFS) declines by more than 1% in the same month, it indicates a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < 1.2 million AND RSAFS declines > 1% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in CPI (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% per month for three consecutive months signals inflationary pressure, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as real returns are eroded.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 300,000 in a month signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the positive signal.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5% and real GDP (GDPC1) declines for two consecutive quarters, it indicates a restrictive monetary policy combined with economic contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 5% AND GDPC1 declines for 2 consecutive quarters
regime_hint: economic contraction with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal.
